solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sluggish? It could be the garlic

indicators.note: says the letters of the following words could be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: A cook wonders whether eating garlic is what makes one feel so sluggish.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargic is a direct synonym of sluggish: slow and lacking energy.

clue.text: Lean minor lacking energy

parts.note: to lean is to list, as a ship tilting to one side
minor means less, smaller or lesser

explanation.surface: A thin youngster is described as having no get-up-and-go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lean' looks like an adjective (thin) but works as a verb, tilt; 'minor' looks like a child but means smaller.
explanation.definitionFit: Listless is a synonym describing someone without vigour or enthusiasm.

clue.text: Secure line? Not completely

indicators.note: means the word for line loses its final letter, so it is not given in full

parts.note: a tier is a row or line, as of seats

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a rope has been fastened, and is told it is only partly done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not completely' drops the last letter R from TIER.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie something is to fasten or make it secure, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Fire-raising clergyman beheaded

indicators.note: means the word for clergyman loses its first letter, its head

parts.note: a parson is a parish clergyman

explanation.surface: A vicar who set fires is executed by beheading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beheaded' removes the P from PARSON.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson is the crime of deliberately setting property alight; the clue's compound noun names that act.

clue.text: All-out action?

parts.note: all-out sounds like maximum effort, but here it means everyone walking out of work at once

explanation.surface: A question about going full tilt in some campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All-out' reads as total effort; cryptically it means all the workers coming out on strike together.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoppage by workers across every industry is a nationwide walkout, literally everyone out.

clue.text: Check colour in room

parts.note: CH is the chess abbreviation for check
amber is a yellowish-orange colour

explanation.surface: Someone inspects the paint shade used in a room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check' looks like a verb, but it is the chess term abbreviated CH.
explanation.definitionFit: A chamber is an old or formal word for a room, especially a bedroom.

clue.text: Popular new tavern

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A recently opened pub is drawing crowds.
explanation.definitionFit: A tavern and an inn are both establishments selling drink, often with lodging.

clue.text: Nice surprisingly keeping German city at bottom

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the city inside them
means the letters of the French resort's name end up in an unexpected order

parts.note: Essen is a city in the Ruhr, Germany

explanation.surface: Nice, the French city, unexpectedly hosts a German city in last place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the Riviera city, not the adjective; 'surprisingly' makes INCE, which 'keeping' wraps round the Ruhr city. 'at bottom' is the definition, not a placing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean fundamentally, considered at the most basic level.

clue.text: Do, perhaps, brief correspondence

definitions.meaning: do (doh) is the first ... of the sol-fa scale, an example of a musical tone

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether to dash off a short letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like the verb but is the musical syllable; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Do is a musical tone in sol-fa, and a short written message is also called by the same word.

clue.text: Let it stand next to boy's hat

parts.note: stet is the proofreader's mark meaning let it stand, cancelling a correction
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: An instruction to leave a lad's headwear where it is.
explanation.walkthrough: STET is Latin for 'let it stand', used by editors.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stetson is a broad-brimmed cowboy hat, an example of the category.

clue.text: Fend off a check pinning rook

indicators.note: in chess a piece pins another; here the word for check holds the rook inside it

parts.note: to vet is to check or examine
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A chess player escapes an attack by a check that pins the rook.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess setting is camouflage: 'check' is VET and 'pinning' places R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert a danger is to ward it off or prevent it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Large public school gave the game away

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing
Eton is a famous English public (fee-paying) school

explanation.surface: A big private school leaked secrets.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'public school' is an elite fee-paying school such as Eton.
explanation.definitionFit: To let on is an idiom for revealing a secret, the same as spilling the beans.

clue.text: Score not yet attained by this youth group

definitions.text: Score not yet attained by this youth group

parts.words: Score not yet attained by this youth group
parts.note: a score is twenty; people aged thirteen to nineteen have not reached that age

explanation.surface: A youth team has not yet managed to score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' suggests a goal, but it is the number twenty: the group are all under twenty years old.
explanation.definitionFit: Young people aged thirteen to nineteen are named by the -teen in their ages.

clue.text: Sturdy vehicle showing external decay

indicators.note: the word for decay appears on the outside, wrapped around the vehicle

parts.note: rot means decay
a bus is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A tough old van with rust on its bodywork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing external' means the decay word sits on the outside, wrapped round the vehicle, like rust on a bodywork.
explanation.definitionFit: Robust is a synonym meaning strong and solidly built.

clue.text: Rustic ringing foot of heath bird

indicators.note: the countryman surrounds the next letter, as a ring encircles

parts.note: a rustic is a country person, a peasant

indicators.note: the foot is the bottom, so in a down clue it is the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A countryman encircles the bottom of the moor while shooting a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringing' puts H, the last letter of 'heath', inside PEASANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A pheasant is a long-tailed game bird, an example of the category.

clue.text: Bishop arrested by nervous Lancashire PC in police department

indicators.note: the bishop is held inside, caught by the jumbled letters
the letters of the county and constable are agitated into a new order

parts.note: taken as written; PC is a police constable
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A churchman is taken in by a jittery northern constable working for the force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nervous' rearranges LANCASHIREPC; 'arrested by' puts B inside. Lancashire is an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Special Branch is the name of the British police unit handling national security matters.

clue.text: One about to touch down in European republic

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
re means about or concerning
to land is to touch down, as an aircraft

explanation.surface: A passenger about to arrive on a flight into a European country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as 'on the point of', but 'about' is RE and 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Republic of Ireland is an independent state in western Europe.

clue.text: Mourn the French soldiers taken at the front

parts.note: la is a French word for the
men means soldiers, as in officers and men

indicators.note: picks the first letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Grieve for the French troops captured on the battlefield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the front' sounds military, but it takes the T of 'taken'.
explanation.definitionFit: To lament is a verb synonym meaning to grieve or express sorrow.

clue.text: Article by team's leader, a Greek character

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece beside a captain's profile of a Greek personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' means letter, not person: 'leader' takes T from 'team's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet; character here means written letter.

clue.text: Husband entering word for a unit of heat

indicators.note: the husband goes into the word that follows

parts.note: a term is a word or expression

explanation.surface: A husband walks in with a word about a heating bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' puts H inside TERM.
explanation.definitionFit: A therm is a measure of heat energy, used in gas billing.

clue.text: "Woman" — song about daughter

indicators.note: the song is placed around the next letter

parts.note: a lay is an old word for a song or ballad

explanation.surface: A song titled 'Woman' that is about a daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' means around, not concerning: LAY goes around D.
explanation.definitionFit: A lady is a polite word for a woman, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Some popular enactments here?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Asking whether this is a venue where crowd-pleasing performances are staged.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'here?': the whole clue also describes the place where popular shows are performed.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a venue for public spectacles, so it is where such performances take place.

clue.text: A tendency to do nothing at home I rate badly

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: says the letters of the words before it are put in a poor, disordered arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to rating their own idleness at home poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges I RATE as ERTIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is sluggishness or resistance to action, a disposition to stay still.

clue.text: Short stole? Very

indicators.note: means the word for stole is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: took means stole, as a thief took something

explanation.surface: A shawl that is too short, apparently very much so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stole' looks like a scarf, but is the past tense of steal: TOOK, cut to TOO.
explanation.definitionFit: Too and very are both intensifiers, as in 'not too bad' meaning 'not very bad'.

clue.text: Extras bowled disregarded, of course

indicators.note: means that letter is left out of the word for extras

parts.note: byes are extras in cricket, runs scored without the bat touching the ball
B is the cricket abbreviation for bowled

explanation.surface: A cricket scorer ignores the extras and the bowled dismissals as a matter of course.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, byes are runs conceded as extras; removing B leaves YES.
explanation.definitionFit: Of course is an emphatic affirmation, equivalent to agreeing outright.

clue.text: Very attractive person met abroad in resort

indicators.note: read as re-sort: the letters are sorted again into a new order

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker meets a gorgeous stranger at a foreign seaside resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'resort' read as re-sort is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamboat is informal for someone strikingly good-looking, the object of romantic fantasy.
